user.title: Connect your Powerwall
user.description:
LibrePower talks to the Gateway directly over your local network. You only need the Gateway password printed on the Powerwall itself — no Tesla account required.

Your Home Assistant host must be able to reach the Gateway. If 192.168.91.1 doesn't respond, you may need a static route or to join the Gateway's WiFi network.

amber.title: Amber Electric
amber.description: Create a token at app.amber.com.au → Settings → API.

globird.title: GloBird tariff
globird.description: GloBird doesn't publish a price API, so enter the rates from your bill in dollars per kWh, GST inclusive. You can add peak and off-peak windows afterwards in the integration options.

reauth_confirm.title: Powerwall password changed
reauth_confirm.description: The Gateway is no longer accepting the stored password. Re-enter the password printed on the Powerwall.

error.invalid_gateway_password: The Gateway rejected that password. Check the sticker on the Powerwall — it's the full string, not just the last few characters.
error.gateway_unreachable: Couldn't reach the Gateway at that address. Check that Home Assistant has a network route to it.
error.amber_unavailable: Couldn't reach the Amber API. Try again shortly.
error.no_amber_sites: That Amber account has no sites on it.
error.unknown: Unexpected error — check the Home Assistant logs.

init.title: Control
init.description: While this is off, LibrePower runs in shadow mode: it plans a full schedule and publishes it to sensors, but never writes to the battery. That makes it safe to run alongside PowerSync or any other optimiser.

data.control_enabled: Allow LibrePower to control the battery

confirm_control.title: Hand control to LibrePower?
confirm_control.description:
Only one integration may control a battery. If PowerSync (or anything else) is still managing this Powerwall, disable its optimiser first and confirm it has stopped writing.

This also requires v1r pairing (a one-time Fleet API key registration) - the same step PowerSync itself uses for control. Gateway-password-only setup can plan a schedule but cannot write it; enabling control without v1r configured will show 'Control enabled, but v1r pairing is required' on the integration.

Two optimisers on one battery will fight: each reads the other's change as an error and corrects it, and the battery cycles needlessly.

Leave the box unticked to stay in shadow mode.

data.understood: No other integration is controlling this Powerwall

battery.title: Battery and optimiser
battery.description:
Wear cost charges the optimiser for battery throughput so it won't chase arbitrage that costs more in cell degradation than it earns. Around 0.02 $/kWh is a reasonable starting point for LFP; set 0 to disable.

Weather-aware solar forecasting uses Open-Meteo (no account or API key needed) to adjust the history-based solar forecast for tomorrow's actual weather, rather than just typical conditions for the season. Off by default - the history-based forecast works fully offline either way; this only sharpens it. If Open-Meteo is unreachable, the integration silently falls back to history-only.
